front: Are the project management principles rules?
back: No. They are not prescriptive. They guide mindset and behavior, and how they apply depends on context.
Adopt a Holistic View; Focus on Value; Embed Quality Into Processes and Deliverables; Be an Accountable Leader; Integrate Sustainability Within All Project Areas; Build an Empowered Culture.

front: Three dimensions of the project management mindset
back: Proactive, ownership, value-driven.
Adopt a Holistic View and Embed Quality Into Processes and Deliverables.
Be an Accountable Leader and Build an Empowered Culture.
Focus on Value and Integrate Sustainability Within All Project Areas.
Principles are the mindset. Performance domains are the mechanics: the knowledge, processes and methods that put principles into practice.
Governance, Scope (including quality), Schedule, Finance, Stakeholders, Resources, Risk.

front: Can two principles contradict each other?
back: No. They complement one another and may overlap, but none contradicts another.
Understand and manage the project by considering all components and their interdependencies as part of a larger system.
Seeing the interconnectedness of elements: relationships and patterns in full context, not static snapshots. Helps find root causes.
Continually evaluate and adjust the project's alignment with business objectives and intended benefits. Value is the ultimate indicator of success.

front: What should happen if a project can no longer deliver its intended value?
back: It may be best to terminate it.
During the project, at the end of the project, or after completion.
The software is the output. Higher productivity is the outcome. Training may be the extra deliverable that makes the outcome happen.
The document holding the project justification and link to strategy. It guides decisions toward the intended business value.
The degree to which the inherent characteristics of a deliverable or process help meet or exceed the project's target objectives.
Conformance to acceptance criteria, the definition of done (DoD), fitness for use, and overall efficiency.
Continuous improvement and waste elimination.

front: Quality activities for the product vs for the process
back: Product: training, inspections, testing. Process: reviews and audits. Both aim to prevent errors and defects.
Putting quality practices as early in the project life cycle as possible.
People, profit and planet.

front: Which performance domain is most strongly tied to quality?
back: Scope. In the 8th edition the Scope domain includes quality.
